s1.syndrome_frame: Sudden onset of severe, episodic, sharp, electric-shock–like pain on one side of the face, localized to specific nerve distributions, triggered by specific actions, with associated sensory disturbances
salient_findings: Severe pain on the left side of the face
Pain localized to V2 and V3 distributions of the left trigeminal nerve
Attacks triggered by jaw movement during eating or tooth brushing
Allodynia to cold air and hypersensitivity to touch in the affected area
key_facts: 36-year-old woman
Pain started after receiving the third dose of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine
Pain initially affected the entire left hemiface
Attacks last 4–5 seconds
Pain reaches 10/10 on a numeric pain scale
Distorted sensations in the V2 region during attacks
Sensory testing is otherwise normal
No other neurological deficits
No relevant past medical or family history
Prior doses of the same vaccine were uneventful
Routine laboratory tests, including D-dimer, are normal
RT-qPCR for SARS-CoV-2 and other infections is negative
Contrast-enhanced MRI of the head shows no abnormalities

shortlist.label: Trigeminal neuralgia
shortlist.why_kept: Severe, episodic, sharp, electric-shock–like pain on one side of the face, localized to specific nerve distributions, triggered by specific actions

shortlist.label: Classical trigeminal neuralgia
shortlist.why_kept: Pain characteristics and distribution match classical trigeminal neuralgia, with no apparent secondary cause

shortlist.label: Secondary trigeminal neuralgia
shortlist.why_kept: Possible relationship to COVID-19 vaccine, although rare, warrants consideration of secondary causes

shortlist.label: Glossopharyngeal neuralgia
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, glossopharyngeal neuralgia can present with similar pain characteristics and should be considered in the differential

shortlist.label: Postherpetic neuralgia
shortlist.why_kept: Given the recent vaccine administration and potential for vaccine-related complications, postherpetic neuralgia is a plausible, albeit less common, diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of episodic, sharp, electric-shock–like pain in the V2 and V3 distributions of the left trigeminal nerve, triggered by jaw movement, and reaching 10/10 on a numeric pain scale, are characteristic of classical trigeminal neuralgia. The absence of other neurological deficits, normal sensory testing, and lack of abnormalities on contrast-enhanced MRI of the head also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Trigeminal neuralgia
rejected.why: Too broad, as classical trigeminal neuralgia is a more specific diagnosis that fits the patient's symptoms

rejected.label: Secondary trigeminal neuralgia
rejected.why: No evidence of an underlying cause, such as a tumor or multiple sclerosis, and normal MRI results

rejected.label: Glossopharyngeal neuralgia
rejected.why: Pain is localized to the trigeminal nerve distribution, not the glossopharyngeal nerve distribution

rejected.label: Postherpetic neuralgia
rejected.why: No history of herpes zoster infection, and RT-qPCR for SARS-CoV-2 and other infections is negative
